paragraphs.source_en: It helps for someone to function as a “host” to shift the group from chatting to the topic at hand. The host may get the ball rolling by starting the first go-round and also initiate the final go-round about ten to fifteen minutes from the agreed ending. Hosts are part of the conversation. They don’t lob in firecracker questions from the edge to see what happens, or offer advice. They stay curious, inquisitive, and open along with everyone.

paragraphs.source_en: An open-ended question or suggestion that everyone can answer from their own experience works best. Use the questions at the end of each chapter, and then try to come up with your own. Remember, implied in many questions and topics is “. . . and why?” Don’t be afraid to go there. A great way to drive a question deeper is for someone to say, “Tell me more about that,” or “What led you to that point of view?” Be careful, because your tone matters. “Why do you think that?” can sound truly interested or quite snarky.
